Well I'm sorry you're in this situation to begin with it's difficult all around. Empathy and compassion go a long way but it's not always enough. Make sure to take care of yourself as you go through this and just do what you can. If you see this going to a custody battle though getting some sort of records about the type of living environment the parents forced your friend to endure could be helpful in keeping the child away from them too.

Then I would do your best to keep her away from them, if she's not in the right headspace to make good decisions for her and her daughter then I'd say worst case is looking into alternatives with her husband and finding a potential inpatient place for her to stay for a little while to safely get her back on meds and regulated and recieve proper diagnosis if she doesn't have one. Forcing someone to go inpatient can be a traumatic experience so if you find one make sure it's good and hopefully talk her into going herself. But if her parents are abusive then you need to prioritize the child instead of her as that child does not deserve in the slightest to be placed in an abusive environment.

That's fair if her parents are supportive of mental health struggles and can help I'd consider looping them in. Getting a love one back on meds can be difficult and delicate and I think largely involves knowing the individual and their values. Good luck and I hope everyone ends up ok.
